dates.notes: Signed by New Zealand, Chile and Singapore on 11 June 2020 GMT (12 June 2020 New Zealand time). Entered into force for New Zealand and Singapore on 7 January 2021 and for Chile on 23 November 2021. Korea's accession took effect on 3 May 2024. Costa Rica presented its Instrument of Accession in New Zealand on 17 July 2026; Chile's SUBREI page records its accession as effective on 14 September 2026, and the joint release dated 17 September 2026 welcomes it as the fifth Party without stating a date. The New Zealand MFAT overview still says four Parties and lists Costa Rica as invited; it is older than the September 2026 release. A Protocol to the DEPA was signed on 15 July 2023; sources differ between 19 and 20 March 2024 for its entry into force.

ai_provisions: Article 8.2 — Artificial Intelligence: recognition of AI's economic and social importance; promotion of ethical and governance frameworks; consideration of internationally recognised principles including explainability, transparency, fairness and human-centred values
relevance.excluded_scope: The AI article does not create enforceable substantive standards, conformity assessment or market-access conditions; it commits the Parties to promote and endeavour.
relevance.reason: A binding digital-economy agreement whose Module 8 contains a dedicated article on artificial intelligence. The AI provision is expressly included in a treaty, although its operative language is cooperative and best-efforts ('shall endeavour'), not a set of prohibitions or product rules.
